result.title: LiteSTAR: Low-Rank Channel Modulation for Temporally Consistent CVD Video Compensation
result.summary: Color Vision Deficiency (CVD) affects a large population worldwide, yet practical recoloring must run continuously on-device. Frame-wise video recoloring produces color flickering, while existing methods rely on costly cross-frame alignment in pixel or feature space. We observe that color flickering correlates with variations in channel-wise responses, with color-sensitive variations concentrated in a low-rank subspace. Based on this observation, we propose Lightweight Spatio-Temporal Adaptive Recoloring (LiteSTAR), built around LiCaD, a plug-and-play Lightweight Channel-Adaptive Decoder. LiCaD performs temporal filtering in a low-rank state space with learned process and observation uncertainties. It then modulates feature channels to achieve temporal consistency without explicit spatial alignment. LiteSTAR further employs adaptive patch routing to improve color discrimination for CVD users while avoiding unnecessary over-enhancement. We also introduce EgoCVDSet, the first egocentric video benchmark for CVD recoloring. Extensive quantitative and qualitative experiments demonstrate that LiteSTAR achieves superior performance with only 0.05M parameters. LiCaD further demonstrates strong generalization across different tasks and network architectures. The code, models, and dataset will be released after review.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 LiteSTAR，以可插拔的轻量通道自适应解码器 LiCaD 在低秩状态空间中做时序滤波并调制特征通道，实现色觉缺陷（CVD）视频重着色的一致性与低参数量。
AI.relevance_reason: 其用学习到的过程／观测不确定性在低秩空间更新隐状态、再据此调制特征的做法，可能为 LVR 中跨步 latent 状态维护与更新提供可核查线索；但任务是辅助性视频重着色，不涉及多模态推理本身。
